analysis_trace: Trial NCT05914038 is a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group study comparing individualized rTMS (guided by fNIRS lateralization index) versus traditional rTMS in stroke patients with upper limb motor impairment (MRC ≤3) within 3 months of stroke onset. Primary endpoint is Fugl-Meyer Assessment at 12 weeks.

Evidence base: Meta-analysis (Alhalabi et al., 2025) shows rTMS significantly improves FMA-UE with SMD 1.28 (95% CI 0.74-1.82) in subacute stroke. Effect sizes are larger with 15-20 sessions. Network meta-analysis shows rTMS effect size 2.58 (95% CI 0.18-4.97) for motor outcomes.

Individualized rTMS approach: fNIRS-guided targeting based on lateralization index is mechanistically rational but limited direct RCT evidence. fNIRS-rTMS integration studies show feasibility for dynamic monitoring. One related trial (NCT04617366) uses similar individualized approach.
Population match: Subacute stroke (within 3 months), moderate-severe impairment (MRC ≤3), age >20. Matches evidence base well. Sample size 40 is small but typical for rTMS stroke trials.

Primary endpoint (FMA-UE, 12 weeks): Based on meta-analytic evidence, rTMS shows consistent improvement. Predict mean difference ~8-12 points favoring individualized rTMS over traditional rTMS. Confidence moderate due to small sample and novel individualized approach.

Secondary endpoints: MRC Scale (muscle strength) - expected improvement correlating with FMA gains. NIHSS - expected modest improvement. Barthel Index - expected improvement in ADL. Modified Rankin Scale - expected shift toward lower scores. MEP - expected improved corticospinal excitability. FMA at 1/4 weeks - earlier timepoints show smaller gains. fNIRS - cortical activation changes expected.
Safety: rTMS generally well-tolerated in stroke. Seizure risk low with standard protocols. No major safety concerns anticipated.

Key uncertainties: (1) Individualized fNIRS-guided targeting vs traditional rTMS efficacy difference not established in RCTs; (2) Small sample size (n=40) limits power; (3) Optimal lateralization index threshold undefined; (4) 12-week follow-up may miss late responders.

Evidence role assignments: Alhalabi 2025 meta-analysis = indirect_direction (same drug/rTMS, same indication/stroke, same endpoint/FMA-UE, different protocol/individualized vs standard); numeric_use_allowed = range estimate only. fNIRS-rTMS integration papers = mechanism_background; numeric_use_allowed = false. NCT04617366 = indirect_direction (similar design); numeric_use_allowed = false due to protocol differences.

fNIRS-rTMS integration feasible for stroke rehabilitation monitoring
fNIRS can guide rTMS targeting in stroke

value.estimand: difference in Fugl-Meyer Assessment upper extremity score at 12 weeks post-intervention, individualized rTMS vs traditional rTMS, ITT population
value.uncertainty: No direct RCT evidence for individualized fNIRS-guided rTMS vs traditional rTMS; estimate based on meta-analysis of standard rTMS vs sham/control. Small sample size (n=40) increases variability. Novel targeting approach may enhance or limit efficacy.
value.rationale: Meta-analysis shows rTMS improves FMA-UE with large effect size (SMD 1.28) in subacute stroke. Individualized targeting based on fNIRS lateralization index is mechanistically rational but unproven. Predict 8-12 point improvement favoring individualized approach.

value.estimand: change in MRC Scale for Muscle Strength at 12 weeks post-intervention, individualized rTMS vs traditional rTMS
value.uncertainty: MRC scale correlates with FMA but less sensitive; limited specific data on rTMS effects on MRC. Small sample size.
value.rationale: Expected improvement in muscle strength correlating with FMA gains. MRC grade improvement typically 0.5-1.5 grades with motor recovery interventions in subacute stroke.

value.estimand: change in NIH Stroke Scale at 12 weeks post-intervention, lower scores indicate better outcome
value.uncertainty: NIHSS primarily measures stroke severity, less sensitive to motor-specific interventions. Mixed evidence for rTMS effects on NIHSS.
value.rationale: Modest NIHSS improvement expected as motor function improves. Less pronounced than FMA changes due to scale focus on multiple neurological domains.

value.estimand: change in Barthel Index at 12 weeks post-intervention, higher scores indicate better outcome
value.uncertainty: ADL improvements lag behind motor gains; ceiling effects possible. Limited specific rTMS data on Barthel Index.
value.rationale: Expected improvement in activities of daily living following motor recovery. Meta-analysis showed rTMS improves functional independence measures.

value.estimand: distribution shift in Modified Rankin Scale at 12 weeks post-intervention, lower scores indicate better outcome
value.uncertainty: mRS may show floor/ceiling effects in subacute stroke; shift analysis more appropriate than mean difference.
value.rationale: Expected shift toward lower disability grades with motor recovery. Effect may be modest given subacute stage and baseline severity.

value.estimand: change in motor evoked potential amplitude at 12 weeks post-intervention
value.uncertainty: MEP highly variable; depends on coil positioning and individual cortical excitability. fNIRS guidance may improve targeting consistency.
value.rationale: rTMS modulates corticospinal excitability; MEP amplitude expected to increase with effective stimulation. Individualized targeting may enhance neurophysiological response.

value.estimand: difference in Fugl-Meyer Assessment at 4 weeks post-intervention
value.uncertainty: Earlier timepoint shows smaller treatment effect than 12 weeks; spontaneous recovery contributes substantially at 4 weeks.
value.rationale: FMA gains at 4 weeks expected to be approximately half of 12-week gains based on typical recovery trajectories in subacute stroke.

value.estimand: change in cortical activation patterns measured by fNIRS at 12 weeks post-intervention
value.uncertainty: fNIRS is intervention guidance tool; changes expected but clinical significance unclear. High measurement variability.
value.rationale: fNIRS-guided intervention designed to rebalance interhemispheric activation. Expected shift in lateralization index toward more normalized pattern with individualized targeting.

trial_outcome_prediction.rationale: rTMS has established efficacy for motor recovery in subacute stroke per meta-analyses. Individualized fNIRS-guided approach is mechanistically rational though not yet proven superior. Primary endpoint (FMA-UE) likely to show improvement based on evidence base. Small sample size and novel protocol introduce uncertainty but overall probability of positive trial outcome is moderate-to-high.
